faq: Why not just split by page count?

Because a page's size is not uniform: one scanned or image-heavy page can weigh more than thirty text pages. Splitting a 60-page scan into three chunks of 20 pages routinely produces parts of 4 MB, 9 MB and 31 MB. Measuring each part as it is written is the only way to know it fits.
What happens when one page is larger than the limit?

It is written on its own, and the tool names the page and its size. No split can make a single page smaller — that needs image recompression — so if the limit is strict, compress the PDF first and split the result.
Are the parts still complete PDFs?

Yes. Each part is a standalone document with its own cross-reference table, so it opens on its own in any reader. The outline is not carried over: a part is a new document that starts on its first page.

faq: Does PDF to Text work on scanned PDFs?
Not on the text itself — a scan is a picture with no text layer, so there is nothing to copy. The tool tells you when pages are scans; run OCR PDF first and the recognised text can then be extracted.
Is the layout preserved in the .txt file?
The reading order and line breaks of the text layer are kept, but columns, tables and images are not reproduced. For layout, use PDF to Word or PDF to JPG.

faq: Does it capture text and vector graphics?
No. This tool extracts embedded raster images only — text, tables and vector shapes are not pictures, so nothing is produced for them. Use PDF to PNG if you need a picture of the whole page.
Why are some images missing from the ZIP?

Images smaller than 16 pixels are skipped because they are page decoration, not content, and a very large image (above 40 megapixels) is skipped rather than crashing the browser tab. Both are counted in the summary.

faq: Does PDF to CSV work on scanned tables?

No. A scan is a picture: there are no text runs to group into rows, so nothing is detected. Run OCR PDF first and the recognised text can then be turned into a table. When nothing is found the tool says "no table found" rather than exporting an empty or one-column file.
What happens to merged cells and cells with two lines of text?

CSV cannot express a cell that spans two columns, so the value is written once and the next column stays empty. Text that wraps onto two lines becomes two rows. Check the first few rows before you rely on the file.
The columns are misaligned — why?

Detection reads the space between runs, so columns that sit very close together, or right-aligned numbers of very different widths, can land in the wrong cell. Comparing the first rows against the page is the quickest way to spot it; a table with a clear gutter between columns converts cleanly.

faq: Why is a cell 1,024 instead of 1024?

Because that is what the page says. A value with a thousands separator, a currency symbol or a leading zero is written as text so it stays exactly as printed; only plain numbers become numeric cells, which is what keeps a SUM honest.
Can all the tables go on one worksheet?

Not directly: one worksheet per page keeps each table's columns meaning what they meant on its own page, and stacking them would misalign the columns. Copy the sheets into one in Excel if you need them side by side.
Why is there no formatting in the workbook?
This tool moves data, not layout: no bold, no fills, no merged ranges, no colour copied from the PDF. What you get is a sheet you can carry on calculating in.

faq: How do I print it?
Double-sided, flip on the SHORT edge, no scaling (100%). Fold the stack in half and staple twice on the spine.
What is a signature?
The number of pages folded together. 16 pages is a comfortable booklet; a 200-page document becomes thirteen 16-page signatures.
Why did blank pages appear?
A signature must hold a multiple of four pages. Blanks are added at the end of the last signature — never in the middle, which would shift every page after the gap.
What is binding creep?
On thick booklets the inner pages sit further from the fold. Creep shifts the two halves outward by the millimetres you enter; leave it at 0 for thin booklets.
